issues.legal_issue: A land acquisition authority must complete the acquisition process within a reasonable time even when no express deadline governs the making of an award, and unjustified delay can warrant additional compensation where the statutory valuation date leaves the owner with compensation based on a substantially earlier market value.
material_facts: The acquisition declarations were followed by awards only after a delay of many years.
The authority did not adequately explain its failure to take effective steps to make awards after the challenges to the acquisition had been dismissed.
Compensation was determined by reference to the market value at the date of the original notifications, substantially earlier than the dates of the awards.
The affected owners were small cultivators, and the delay caused them injury because land values had escalated.
issues.conclusion: The authority failed to perform its statutory duty within a reasonable time. Rather than quash the acquisitions, the Court directed additional compensation, calculated by reference to the market value at the original notification date, for the period after the reasonable time for making awards had expired until the awards were made.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory power for which no time limit is prescribed must be exercised within a reasonable time, assessed in light of the circumstances and nature of the power (State of Gujarat v. Pastel Raghav Natha; Mansaram v. S.P. Pathak). Acquisition proceedings should be completed expeditiously after a declaration, without unreasonable delay (State of Madhya Pradesh v. Vishnu Prasad Sharma; Ambalal Purshottam v. Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation; Khadim Hussain v. State of U.P.). The second proviso to Article 31A and Sections 11(1) and 23(1) of the Land Acquisition Act informed the Court's concern that delayed awards based on an old notification-date value could fail to secure the required market-value compensation. The Court relied on its remedial powers under Articles 32 and 226 to grant additional compensation.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and awards_delayed_for_an_unreasonable_period and not authority_provided_adequate_justification and compensation_based_on_substantially_earlier_market_value

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The case concerns compulsory acquisition of land and the completion of the acquisition process.
predicates.awards_delayed_for_an_unreasonable_perio: The authority took an unreasonable length of time after the acquisition declaration to make the awards.
predicates.authority_provided_adequate_justificatio: The authority gave an adequate explanation for the delay in making the awards.
predicates.compensation_based_on_substantially_earl: The compensation was determined using a market value substantially earlier than the time when the awards were made.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition award is unreasonably delayed without adequate justification and compensation uses a substantially earlier market value, additional compensation is awarded.

issues.legal_issue: A later statutory deadline for making acquisition awards does not validate earlier unreasonable inaction or apply to awards already made before that deadline took effect.
material_facts: The acquisition declarations predated the 1984 amendment that introduced a deadline for making awards.
The awards in the proceedings at issue had been made before the amendment came into force.
The authority argued that the amendment's transitional deadline validated the earlier delay.
issues.conclusion: The transitional deadline did not validate or justify the earlier delay, and it did not apply to proceedings in which awards had already been made before the amendment came into force.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11-A of the Land Acquisition Act introduced a deadline for making awards. Its proviso set a transitional deadline for declarations published before the amendment, but the proviso did not retrospectively validate earlier inaction and did not apply where the awards had already been made before commencement of the amendment.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The case concerns compulsory acquisition of land and the completion of the acquisition process.
predicates.delay_occurred_before_later_award_deadli: The authority's delay in making the award occurred before a later statutory deadline for awards took effect.
predicates.award_made_before_later_deadline_took_ef: The authority made the award before the later statutory deadline took effect.

issues.definition: In an acquisition proceeding, a later award deadline does not validate earlier delay when the award was already made before that deadline took effect.

issues.legal_issue: When acquisition proceedings have been left unchallenged for a long time and the acquired land has been developed for public use, quashing the acquisition may be inappropriate even though the authority's delay was unjustified; modified monetary relief may instead be granted.
material_facts: The owners sought relief only after a long period had passed.
By then, the land had been taken into possession and developed or put to public use, including use for housing and planned development.
Third-party interests had arisen and those third parties were not before the Court.
The authority had not justified its prolonged failure to complete the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to quash the acquisition proceedings because doing so would harm public interest and potentially affect third parties. It held that the owners' delay in seeking relief had to be considered alongside the authority's inaction and granted modified monetary relief instead.
issues.legal_principle: Delay by a claimant in invoking writ jurisdiction must be considered together with the statutory authority's failure to perform its duties within a reasonable time. Where subsequent development, public use, and third-party interests make quashing inappropriate, a court may grant a modified remedy, including additional compensation, under Articles 32 or 226. The Court referred to Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi, Ramjas Foundation v. Union of India, Special Land Acquisition Officer v. Godrej and Boyce, and its prior use of remedial powers in Ujjain Vikas Pradhikaran v. Raj Kumar Johri, Akhara Brahm Buta v. State of Punjab, Bihar State Housing Board v. Ban Bihari Mahato, and Union Carbide Corporation v. Union of India.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and authority_delay_unjustified and claimant_waited_a_long_time_to_seek_relief and land_developed_or_put_to_public_use and third_party_interests_arose

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The case concerns compulsory acquisition of land and the completion of the acquisition process.
predicates.authority_delay_unjustified: The authority failed to complete the acquisition process within a reasonable time and did not adequately justify that failure.
predicates.claimant_waited_a_long_time_to_seek_reli: The affected owner did not seek judicial relief until a substantial time had passed.
predicates.land_developed_or_put_to_public_use: The acquired land had been developed or used for a public purpose by the time relief was considered.
predicates.third_party_interests_arose: Interests of people who were not before the court had arisen in connection with the acquired land.

issues.definition: When unjustified delay is challenged only after land has been put to public use and third-party interests have arisen, the acquisition is not quashed and modified monetary relief is granted.
